modelName: The constitutional arena — read against the RCN Constitution, which answers more than we assumed and adds an organ we missed
modelNote: REVISED 2026-08-31 after reading the actual RCN Constitution and the RCN Ethical Oversight Framework (ndcgroup.relocalizecreativity.net/rcn-constitution and /rcn-constitution-notes). The first version of this drawing was inferred from code and drawings; the Constitution is the source, and it corrects it three ways. (1) Two rows marked OPEN are settled: Article III §1 gives RCN one class of member, every voice equal; Article II §1 makes founding self-declared. (2) It adds constitutional content the drawing had no node for: fairness as the superordinate condition for all action, and an amendment rule. (3) It adds a constitutional ORGAN — a superordinate ethical metasystem with real veto power over every arena below, per Mick Ashby's Ethical Regulator Theorem. That organ is the reason ethics can be more than personal here: a veto is standing to halt somebody else, and standing is only ever granted constitutionally. Statuses are now sourced, not asserted.

nodes.label: Ethics beyond the personal is standing to halt somebody else. Standing is only ever granted here.
nodes.note: Personal ethics needs no permission — I decline to act. Ethics beyond the personal is an act on another: I stop you, or I require you to answer. That is authority over someone else's action, and no collective-choice arena can grant it to a body meant to constrain that same arena. It has to come from above. Which is Marc's claim, and the reason the RCN Constitution has an ethical metasystem in it rather than a values statement.

nodes.label: FAIRNESS FIRST
nodes.note: "Fairness is our superordinate condition for action. Nothing proceeds at any level without checking for fairness." A rule that gates every band is by definition constitutional, and the first drawing had no node for it at all.

nodes.label: WHO MAY HOLD AN IDENTITY
nodes.note: A person mints their own did:key on their own device, never mentor-held. Settled in engineering before it was settled in text.

nodes.label: WHO MAY FORK
nodes.note: Anyone may fork any page. Article IV: everything we produce is open. Ostrom's first design principle, answered in the affirmative for everyone.

nodes.label: WHO OWNS THE RECORD
nodes.note: Settled for SODOTO: the person, own key, own site. Deliberately deferred for the Shared Care Plan, where the crux is multi-editor rather than single-owner.

nodes.label: ONE CLASS OF MEMBER
nodes.note: CORRECTION. The first drawing marked this OPEN. Article III §1: "All participation in the Network is voluntary. Every voice carries equal weight." That is a class structure — exactly one class — and it is stated. Article II §1 likewise settles founding: an unincorporated network where each member and neighborhood decides for itself, so a node is self-declared and needs nobody's permission. Both were answered; the drawing had simply never read the Constitution.

nodes.label: HOW WE AMEND
nodes.note: Article V §3: a living document, reviewed annually, amended by consensus of active participants. This is the rule Ostrom cares about most — can the group reach and change its own constitutional rules? Answered yes. And it is what stops the ethical veto becoming unaccountable: the watchers are amendable by the membership.

nodes.label: ETHICAL METASYSTEM — SEVEN POINTS OF VIEW
nodes.note: Mick Ashby's Ethical Regulator Theorem made operational. Seven standpoints supply the requisite variety: Future Generations, Adjacent Communities, The Living Environment, The Marginalized Insider, The Informed Outsider, The Historical Record, The Systemic View. Roughly five people per group, minimum three, and every person sits in at least two — which builds information bridges across the whole. Outputs are warnings (the system working), vetoes (the system stopping something), and periodic assessments. In extremis the External Authority is the full RCN membership. NOTE: two structural choices here are load-bearing. Independence cannot be granted by hierarchy in a network that has none, so it is manufactured by publicness — every warning and veto is posted to FedWiki, and transparency IS the independence mechanism. And no PoV outranks another; authority comes from convergence across standpoints, not from a chair.

nodes.label: WHO MAY TEACH
nodes.note: STILL OPEN. The Constitution says nothing about it. In practice holding a badge for X appears to confer standing to teach X — a constitutional rule that operates without being written, and therefore cannot be pointed at, argued with, or amended. It is also the rule that decides whether an NDC can become coordinatorless.

nodes.label: WHAT CLASSES EXIST IN AN NDC
nodes.note: STILL OPEN, and correctly so — the Constitution governs RCN, not the enterprises RCN helps form. The Ethical Oversight Framework says this framework is to be worked out in RCN first, then applied to NDC constitutions, then to RenDanHeYi micro-enterprises. The co-op has a consumer class and a worker class because somebody decided; nothing yet says who may decide there is a third.

nodes.label: RECOGNITION OF THE RIGHT TO ORGANISE
nodes.note: Ostrom's seventh design principle. Whether a county health co-op may contract as agent without an insurance licence is decided in Olympia. The binding constraint nobody in Whatcom can vote on.

nodes.label: PLAN DESIGN
nodes.note: Collective-choice. Decides what is covered and who is paid for what.

nodes.label: CO-OP BOARD
nodes.note: Collective-choice. Elects seats, sets price, wage and the split.

nodes.label: A veto is the whole argument. Values persuade; only a constitution can authorise one person to stop another.
nodes.note: The Framework is precise about this: a warning that redirects a plan is the system working, and a thumbs-down on a completed action is the system failing. Anticipatory, not reactive. Which is only possible because the veto exists — an ethics that can only comment arrives after the harm.

edges.label: the superordinate condition
edges.note: Sourced: RCN Constitution, Ethical Regulation section.

edges.label: even the watchers are amendable — annually, by consensus
edges.note: Article V §3. The answer to who watches the watchers, and the reason the veto is not a new hierarchy.

edges.label: boundary rule — who can be a participant at all
edges.note: No did:key, no badge, no standing anywhere.

edges.label: scope rule — what anyone may copy, anyone may teach
edges.note: Worth checking whether this is true or merely tidy.

edges.label: information rule — who may see the record
edges.note: Information rules govern what a position knows when it chooses.

edges.label: position rule — every voice equal, one class
edges.note: Article III §1. Note this settles RCN and says nothing about the co-op, which is a different constitution not yet written.

edges.label: position rule — operates, UNWRITTEN
edges.note: The cheapest constitutional gap to close: the rule already runs, it simply has never been stated.

edges.label: position rule — which seats exist
edges.note: And this is the constitutional root of the CHW with no seat: you cannot seat someone in a class that does not exist.

edges.label: whether this board may decide at all
VETO
edges.note: Sourced: Ethical Oversight Framework, How Warnings and Vetoes Flow. A veto names the rule violated, the reasoning, and the conditions under which it would be lifted. Silence in response is not acceptable and triggers escalation.

edges.label: VETO
edges.note: Superordinate means over every arena, not a seat in one of them.

edges.label: VETO
edges.note: Contested vetoes go to a cross-PoV convergence, which does not vote — it reads the matter through all seven standpoints.
